ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human reviewer (Trust & Safety): supply the full chat transcript incl. F10–F12, the call log F14, the arrival/GPS record F7/F3 and the timeline F4/F6, and the rider's complaint. Hold the $5.00 no-show fee pending that review; no account or refund action to execute now. (The driver's NS-1 record is otherwise clean; any interim measure is for the reviewer under SAFE-4.)
ruling.reasoning: The driver cancelled at 17:15:30 and the fee on record is $5.00 [F4][F8][F9]. The trace settles the NS-1 mechanics: arrival confirmed by driver tap within 200 m (40 m; closest 38 m) [F7][F1], 330 s of continuous presence from arrival against a 300 s free-wait threshold [F7][F3], two in-app messages (first 17:10:30) and one in-app call (17:11:30) before cancelling [F5][F14], and the rider still absent at cancellation after her 17:12 "2 min, coming" [F11][F4][F6][NS-1]. Those elements are not in issue: both advocates conceded NS-1(i)–(iv) in their rebuttals.

element_findings.reason: The app reason is rider_no_show [F4] and the driver's own words give waiting and the unanswered call as his reason, with no car trouble, other job, personal matter or refusal of the trip [F15][F10][F14]; the rider's 17:12 "2 min, coming" [F11] and her absence at 17:15:30 [F6] match a no-show. The threatening 17:15 message [F12] is not a reason of his own for cancelling under NS-0; on this record the cancellation is the no-show branch, NS-1, not NS-3.

rejected_claims.reason: The NS-1 conditions do hold, but D7 asks the $5.00 to stand as the final outcome [F4][F8][NS-1]; the driver's own message at 17:15, 30 s before he cancelled [F12][F4], is a threat on the record [F13], so under SAFE-1 the case goes to a human and no money outcome may execute now [SAFE-3].

D8 concedes F12 is a threat under SAFE-1 [F12], but it asks the $5.00 fee to be treated as system-final while the safety screen is open [NS-1][TH-2]; once the SAFE-1 screen is open the system may gather evidence and prepare the file only and may not rule [SAFE-3].

C2 is right that a threat in the chat [F12][F13] must be screened and sent to a human [SAFE-1], but the ride money outcome must then wait for that reviewer: the system cannot simultaneously rule that the $5.00 fee is voided or upheld [SAFE-3][NS-1].

C3 asks for interim suspension of the driver pending review [F12][F3][F6][SAFE-4]; whether the accused party is suspended is a decision for the human reviewer after escalation, not a conclusion the system may recommend in a safety case [SAFE-3][SAFE-4].

C7 asks the fee not to stand because the rider was actively coming and the driver was labelled a no-show by the app [F4][F11][F20]; a 17:12 "2 min" message with no arrival by the 17:15:30 cancellation [F6] is the no-show itself, and NS-1 makes the fee turn on its four conditions, not on the rider's intent or the driver's profile [NS-1][SAFE-3].

C9 relies on the rider's clean history and no prior no-shows [F19] to resist the charge [NS-9]; NS-9 is a repeat-no-show flag rule and a clean profile never decides the current case, so it neither voids nor supports the $5.00 fee [NS-9][NS-1].
